title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 12. The Narration of the Slaying of Kamsa and Other Events
html:
Krishnadasa briefly recounts the Mathura pastimes: Kamsa, frightened by evil omens, arranges a contest; Rama and Krishna slay the elephant Kuvalayapida, the wrestlers and Kamsa himself; Nanda returns to Nandishvara and the brothers receive the sacred thread; the Lord, cherishing these pastimes, shows the people of Vraja now a dark form, now a golden one, and each sees in Him their own Krishna — the Lord of their life, in whom Radha and Krishna are one

Verse 1

कृष्णदासस्ततः प्राह शृणु कंसस्य चेष्टितम्।
यत् कृतं तेन दुष्टेन तत् किञ्चित् कथ्यतेऽधुना॥१॥

kṛṣṇadāsastataḥ prāha śṛṇu kaṁsasya ceṣṭitam|
yat kṛtaṁ tena duṣṭena tat kiñcit kathyate'dhunā||1||

krishnadasah — Krishnadasa; tatah — then; praha — said; shrinu — hear; kamsasya — of Kamsa; cheshtitam — the doings; yat — what; kritam — was done; tena — by that; dushtena — villain; tat — of that; kinchit — a little; kathyate — is told; adhuna — now.

1Then Krishnadasa said, "Hear of Kamsa's doings: now something will be told of what that villain did.

Verse 2

मृत्युदूतं बहुविधं दृष्ट्वा रात्रौ सुदुर्मनाः।
कंसो मञ्चादिकं सर्वं कारयामास सत्वरम्॥२॥

mṛtyudūtaṁ bahuvidhaṁ dṛṣṭvā rātrau sudurmanāḥ|
kaṁso mañcādikaṁ sarvaṁ kārayāmāsa satvaram||2||

mrityu-dutam — harbingers of death; bahu-vidham — of many kinds; drishtva — having seen; ratrau — at night; su-durmanah — deeply troubled; kamsah — Kamsa; mancha-adikam — the platforms and the rest; sarvam — all; karayam asa — had made; satvaram — hastily.

2At night Kamsa saw many harbingers of death1, and, deeply troubled, he hastily had the platforms and everything else made ready.

Verse 3

मञ्चोपरिस्थितः सोऽपि चावाह्य बन्धुबान्धवान्।
समानाय्य तदुपरि संस्थाप्य प्राह दुर्मदः॥३॥

mañcoparisthitaḥ so'pi cāvāhya bandhubāndhavān|
samānāyya tadupari saṁsthāpya prāha durmadaḥ||3||

mancha-upari-sthitah — seated on the platform; sah — he; api — too; cha — and; avahya — summoning; bandhu-bandhavan — kinsmen and friends; samanayya — gathering; tat-upari — upon it; samsthapya — seating; praha — said; durmadah — mad with arrogance.

3Seated on the platform, he summoned his kinsmen and friends, gathered them and seated them there too, and, mad with arrogance, he said:

Verse 4

आनीय नन्दं च सगोपवृन्दं निवेश्य मञ्चोपरि सम्भ्रमेण।
कुत्र स्थितौ तौ वरयुद्धकौतुकौ पश्यामि युद्धं च तयोः सुनिर्भरम्॥४॥

ānīya nandaṁ ca sagopavṛndaṁ niveśya mañcopari sambhrameṇa|
kutra sthitau tau varayuddhakautukau paśyāmi yuddhaṁ ca tayoḥ sunirbharam||4||

aniya — bringing; nandam — Nanda; cha — and; sa-gopa-vrindam — with all the cowherds; niveshya — seating; mancha-upari — on the platform; sambhramena — with ceremony; kutra — where; sthitau — are; tau — those two; vara-yuddha-kautukau — eager for a good fight; pashyami — I shall watch; yuddham — the fight; cha — and; tayoh — their; su-nirbharam — to the full.

4'Bring Nanda with all the cowherds and seat them with ceremony on the platform. And where are those two who are so eager for a good fight? I shall watch Them fight to my heart's content!'

Verse 5

ततः परं रामजनार्दनौ प्रभू द्वारस्थितं कुञ्जरराजमेव।
हत्वा च तं तौ च गृहीतदन्तौ प्रजग्मतुरेव सुरङ्गभूमिम्॥५॥

tataḥ paraṁ rāmajanārdanau prabhū dvārasthitaṁ kuñjararājameva|
hatvā ca taṁ tau ca gṛhītadantau prajagmatureva suraṅgabhūmim||5||

tatah param — after that; rama-janardanau — Rama and Janardana; prabhu — the two Lords; dvara-sthitam — stationed at the gate; kunjara-rajam — the king of elephants; eva — indeed; hatva — having slain; cha — and; tam — him; tau — the two; cha — and; grihita-dantau — holding his tusks; prajagmatuh — entered; eva — indeed; su-ranga-bhumim — the splendid arena.

5After that the two Lords, Rama and Janardana, slew the king of elephants stationed at the gate2, and, holding his tusks, They entered the splendid arena.

Verse 6

चाणूरमुष्टी सगणौ निहत्य कंसं च सर्वैरभिनन्दितौ सुखम्।
ततः पितृभ्यामुपलालितौ तौ नन्दं समासाद्य मुदाहतुस्तम्॥६॥

cāṇūramuṣṭī sagaṇau nihatya kaṁsaṁ ca sarvairabhinanditau sukham|
tataḥ pitṛbhyāmupalālitau tau nandaṁ samāsādya mudāhatustam||6||

chanura-mushti — Chanura and Mushtika; sa-ganau — with their followers; nihatya — having slain; kamsam — Kamsa; cha — and; sarvaih — by all; abhinanditau — acclaimed; sukham — joyfully; tatah — then; pitribhyam — by their parents; upalalitau — caressed; tau — the two; nandam — Nanda; samasadya — approaching; muda — joyfully; ahatuh — said; tam — to him.

6Having slain Chanura and Mushtika with their followers, and Kamsa too3, joyfully acclaimed by all and caressed by Their parents, the brothers came to Nanda and cheerfully said to him:

Verse 7

पितः कियन्तं मथुरां दिदृक्षे कालं भवान् मे यदि सुप्रसन्नः।
तदा हि सर्वं सुखमेव मे पितर्मदग्रजो यातु त्वया समं सुखी॥७॥

pitaḥ kiyantaṁ mathurāṁ didṛkṣe kālaṁ bhavān me yadi suprasannaḥ|
tadā hi sarvaṁ sukhameva me pitarmadagrajo yātu tvayā samaṁ sukhī||7||

pitah — father; kiyantam — for some; mathuram — Mathura; didrikshe — I wish to see; kalam — time; bhavan — you; me — towards me; yadi — if; su-prasannah — well disposed; tada — then; hi — indeed; sarvam — all; sukham — happiness; eva — indeed; me — for me; pitah — father; mat-agrajah — my elder brother; yatu — let go; tvaya — you; samam — with; sukhi — happy.

7'Father, if you are well disposed towards Me, I should like to see Mathura for some time. Then, Father, all will be well with Me; and let My elder brother go happily with you.'

Verse 8

श्रुत्वा नन्दो हसन् प्राह बालोऽसि त्वं निरङ्कुशः।
मत्तसिंहसमः केन शमितुं शक्यते भवान्॥८॥

śrutvā nando hasan prāha bālo'si tvaṁ niraṅkuśaḥ|
mattasiṁhasamaḥ kena śamituṁ śakyate bhavān||8||

shrutva — hearing; nandah — Nanda; hasan — laughing; praha — said; balah — a child; asi — are; tvam — you; nirankushah — unbridled; matta-simha-samah — like a maddened lion; kena — by whom; shamitum — to be tamed; shakyate — can; bhavan — you.

8Hearing this, Nanda laughed and said, 'You are an unbridled child, like a maddened lion; who could ever tame You?

Verse 9

बलराम पुनश्चात्र भवान् हि स्थातुमर्हति।
यथा गवां चारणार्थं वृन्दावनगतः क्वचित्॥९॥

balarāma punaścātra bhavān hi sthātumarhati|
yathā gavāṁ cāraṇārthaṁ vṛndāvanagataḥ kvacit||9||

balarama — O Balarama; punah — also; cha — and; atra — here; bhavan — you; hi — indeed; sthatum — to stay; arhati — ought; yatha — as; gavam — the cows; charana-artham — to graze; vrindavana-gatah — gone to Vrindavana; kvachit — at times.

9And You too, Balarama, ought to stay here — just as You used to go off at times to Vrindavana to graze the cows.'4

Verse 10

समालिङ्ग्य सुखेनैव ताभ्यां वन्दित आदरात्।
ययौ नन्दीश्वरं नन्दः कृष्णरामौ हृदि स्थितौ॥१०॥

samāliṅgya sukhenaiva tābhyāṁ vandita ādarāt|
yayau nandīśvaraṁ nandaḥ kṛṣṇarāmau hṛdi sthitau||10||

samalingya — embracing; sukhena — joyfully; eva — indeed; tabhyam — by the two; vanditah — saluted; adarat — respectfully; yayau — went; nandishvaram — to Nandishvara; nandah — Nanda; krishna-ramau — Krishna and Rama; hridi — in his heart; sthitau — abiding.

10Joyfully embracing Them and receiving Their respectful salutations, Nanda went to Nandishvara — and Krishna and Rama abode in his heart.

Verse 11

ततः परं वसुदेवदेवकी पुत्रयोः किल।
उपवीतं च गायत्रीं दापयामासतुर्मुदा॥११॥

tataḥ paraṁ vasudevadevakī putrayoḥ kila|
upavītaṁ ca gāyatrīṁ dāpayāmāsaturmudā||11||

tatah param — after that; vasudeva-devaki — Vasudeva and Devaki; putrayoh — to their two sons; kila — indeed; upavitam — the sacred thread; cha — and; gayatrim — the Gayatri; dapayam asatuh — had given; muda — joyfully.

11After that Vasudeva and Devaki joyfully had their sons invested with the sacred thread and the Gayatri5.

Verse 12

श्रीकृष्णचरितं केन वर्ण्यते क्षुद्रबुद्धिना।
यत्र ब्रह्मादयः सर्वे मुह्यन्ति पारदर्शिनः॥१२॥

śrīkṛṣṇacaritaṁ kena varṇyate kṣudrabuddhinā|
yatra brahmādayaḥ sarve muhyanti pāradarśinaḥ||12||

shri-krishna-charitam — the deeds of Sri Krishna; kena — by whom; varnyate — are described; kshudra-buddhina — of small understanding; yatra — wherein; brahma-adayah — Brahma and the rest; sarve — all; muhyanti — are bewildered; para-darshinah — who see the far shore.

12Who, with his small understanding, can describe the deeds of Sri Krishna, in which Brahma and all who see the far shore are bewildered?"

Verse 13

एवं हि सूत्ररूपां च लीलां माथुरसम्भवाम्।
मेने भूरितरां कृष्णचैतन्यो रसविग्रहः॥१३॥

evaṁ hi sūtrarūpāṁ ca līlāṁ māthurasambhavām|
mene bhūritarāṁ kṛṣṇacaitanyo rasavigrahaḥ||13||

evam — thus; hi — indeed; sutra-rupam — in the form of a sutra (in brief); cha — and; lilam — the pastime; mathura-sambhavam — that took place in Mathura; mene — esteemed; bhuritaram — very highly; krishna-chaitanyah — Krishna Chaitanya; rasa-vigrahah — rasa embodied.

13Thus Krishna Chaitanya, rasa embodied, held in the highest esteem the Mathura pastimes, told in brief, as in a sutra.

Verse 14

क्वचित् श्यामं क्वचित् पीतं लीलानुकरणं क्वचित्।
जगन्मोहनरूपं च स्वरूपं प्रेमदं प्रभुः॥१४॥

kvacit śyāmaṁ kvacit pītaṁ līlānukaraṇaṁ kvacit|
jaganmohanarūpaṁ ca svarūpaṁ premadaṁ prabhuḥ||14||

kvachit — at times; shyamam — a dark (form); kvachit — at times; pitam — a golden (one); lila-anukaranam — the re-enactment of pastimes; kvachit — at times; jagan-mohana-rupam — the form that enchants the world; cha — and; sva-rupam — His own form; prema-dam — which bestows love; prabhuh — the Lord.

14Now dark, now golden6, now re-enacting the pastimes7, the Lord showed His pure devotees both the form that enchants the world and His own form that bestows love —

Verse 15

दर्शयन् शुद्धभक्तानां मनःश्रवणमङ्गलम्।
नृत्यति गायति रौति हसति धावति सुखम्॥१५॥

darśayan śuddhabhaktānāṁ manaḥśravaṇamaṅgalam|
nṛtyati gāyati rauti hasati dhāvati sukham||15||

darshayan — showing; shuddha-bhaktanam — to His pure devotees; manah-shravana-mangalam — a blessing for mind and ear; nrityati — dances; gayati — sings; rauti — cries out; hasati — laughs; dhavati — runs; sukham — blissfully.

15a blessing for their minds and ears; and blissfully He dances, sings, cries out, laughs and runs.

Verse 16

एवं विहरतस्तस्य सर्वदानन्दरूपिणी।
लीला सर्वव्रजस्थानां प्रादुरासीद् गृहे गृहे॥१६॥

evaṁ viharatastasya sarvadānandarūpiṇī|
līlā sarvavrajasthānāṁ prādurāsīd gṛhe gṛhe||16||

evam — thus; viharatah — as He sported; tasya — His; sarvada — ever; ananda-rupini — made of bliss; lila — the pastime; sarva-vraja-sthanam — for all who dwell in Vraja; pradurasit — appeared; grihe grihe — in house after house.

16As He sported thus, His pastimes, ever full of bliss, appeared to all the dwellers of Vraja in house after house —

Verse 17

पूतनामोक्षणादिश्च व्योमासुरवधान्तिका।
वृन्दावनस्थिता या च या च धामान्तरं गता॥१७॥

pūtanāmokṣaṇādiśca vyomāsuravadhāntikā|
vṛndāvanasthitā yā ca yā ca dhāmāntaraṁ gatā||17||

putana-mokshana-adih — beginning with the deliverance of Putana; cha — and; vyoma-asura-vadha-antika — ending with the slaying of the demon Vyoma; vrindavana-sthita — which took place in Vrindavana; ya — which; cha — and; ya — which; cha — and; dhama-antaram — to another abode; gata — passed.

17those beginning with the deliverance of Putana and ending with the slaying of the demon Vyoma, those that took place in Vrindavana, and those that passed to another abode8.

Verse 18

सा तु सर्वा शक्तिमती सर्वसिद्धिप्रदा सदा।
प्रेमभक्तिप्रदा शश्वत् प्रधाना कृष्णरूपिणी॥१८॥

sā tu sarvā śaktimatī sarvasiddhipradā sadā|
premabhaktipradā śaśvat pradhānā kṛṣṇarūpiṇī||18||

sa — it; tu — indeed; sarva — all; shaktimati — full of power; sarva-siddhi-prada — bestowing every perfection; sada — always; prema-bhakti-prada — bestowing loving devotion; shashvat — eternally; pradhana — supreme; krishna-rupini — Krishna Himself in form.

18And all of them, full of power, ever bestowing every perfection, eternally bestowing loving devotion, are supreme; they are Krishna Himself.

Verse 19

केचिद्बालं नवनीतकरं केऽपि पौगण्डरूपं
श्रीदामाद्यैरुपयमुनकं चारयन्तं च वत्सान्।
कैशोराद्यं नवघनरुचिं वेष्टितं गोपिभिश्च
वंशीन्यस्ताधरकिसलयं गौरचन्द्रं ददर्श॥१९॥

kecidbālaṁ navanītakaraṁ ke'pi paugaṇḍarūpaṁ
śrīdāmādyairupayamunakaṁ cārayantaṁ ca vatsān|
kaiśorādyaṁ navaghanaruciṁ veṣṭitaṁ gopibhiśca
vaṁśīnyastādharakisalayaṁ gauracandraṁ dadarśa||19||

kechit — some; balam — as an infant; navanita-karam — with butter in His hand; ke api — others; pauganda-rupam — in the form of a boy; shridama-adyaih — with Shridama and the others; upa-yamunakam — by the Yamuna; charayantam — grazing; cha — and; vatsan — the calves; kaishora-adyam — in youth and beyond; nava-ghana-rucim — lustrous as a new cloud; veshtitam — surrounded; gopibhih — by the gopis; cha — and; vamshi-nyasta-adhara-kisalayam — with the flute set to His lips, tender as new shoots; gaurachandram — Gaurachandra; dadarsha — saw.

19Some saw Gaurachandra as an infant with butter in His hand, others as a boy9 grazing the calves by the Yamuna with Shridama and the rest, others as a youth lustrous as a new cloud, surrounded by the gopis, with the flute set to His lips, tender as new shoots.

Verse 20

एवं दृष्ट्वा परमरसिकाः श्रीलवृन्दावनस्थाः
सर्वे पक्षिमृगपशुगणा बालवृद्धाश्च हर्षात्।
पश्यन्तः स्वं निजनिजरसैर्ह्लादयन्तः परीताः
राधाकृष्णात्मकमपि निजं मेनिरे प्राणनाथम्॥२०॥

evaṁ dṛṣṭvā paramarasikāḥ śrīlavṛndāvanasthāḥ
sarve pakṣimṛgapaśugaṇā bālavṛddhāśca harṣāt|
paśyantaḥ svaṁ nijanijarasairhlādayantaḥ parītāḥ
rādhākṛṣṇātmakamapi nijaṁ menire prāṇanātham||20||

evam — thus; drishtva — having seen; parama-rasikah — the supreme connoisseurs of rasa; shrila-vrindavana-sthah — the dwellers of glorious Vrindavana; sarve — all; pakshi-mriga-pashu-ganah — the flocks of birds, the deer and the beasts; bala-vriddhah — young and old; cha — and; harshat — out of joy; pashyantah — seeing; svam — their own; nija-nija-rasaih — each with their own rasa; hladayantah — delighting; paritah — surrounding; radha-krishna-atmakam — whose self is Radha and Krishna; api — indeed; nijam — their own; menire — considered; prana-natham — Lord of life.

20So, seeing Him, all the supreme connoisseurs of rasa, the dwellers of glorious Vrindavana — the flocks of birds, the deer and the beasts, young and old — thronging around Him in joy and each delighting Him with their own rasa, saw in Him their own, and took Him, in whom Radha and Krishna are one, as their Lord of life.

Thus ends the twelfth sarga, "The Narration of the Slaying of Kamsa and Other Events" (Kamsa-vadha-adi-varnana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The evil omens described in Bhagavata Purana 10.42.27–31.
  2. The elephant Kuvalayapida (Bhagavata Purana 10.43).
  3. Chanura and Mushtika were Kamsa's wrestlers (ibid. 10.44).
  4. In the Bhagavata Purana (10.45.20–24) Krishna Himself sends Nanda back, promising to return. The sense of v. 9 is not quite clear: Nanda apparently allows Balarama too to stay for a time, as though He had only gone off to the pasture.
  5. Ibid. 10.45.26–29.
  6. Dark is Krishna's form, golden is Gaura's.
  7. That is, acting out Krishna's pastimes in ecstasy.
  8. Putana was the first of the demons slain by Krishna in Vraja (Bhagavata Purana 10.6), Vyoma the last of the asuras of Vraja (ibid. 10.37). "Another abode": Mathura and Dvaraka.
  9. Pauganda is the age from five to ten; kaishora, youth, from ten to sixteen.
